column4: Dr. Elizabeth Russell and Tabytha Wells developed, implemented, and evaluated an intergenerational Psychology of Aging course at Trent University in Winter, 2024 and 2026. This third-year course included and intentionally connected 60 university students and 13 older participants from the community (aged 65+). The classroom aimed to encourage a diverse view of aging while fostering meaningful intergenerational connections through formal lectures and informal intergenerational group activities.

column2: Principle 6: To ensure that the university’s research agenda is informed by the needs of an aging society and to promote public discourse on how higher education can better respond to the varied interests and needs of older adults.,Principle 10: To ensure regular dialogue with organizations representing the interests of the aging population.

column4: The forum's primary purpose is to reframe "well-aging" as a human-rights issue in the era of AI and digital transformation, and to build regional governance dialogue on the digital divide, exclusion, and fundamental rights of older adults. It links Gwangju's human-rights city vision with Chosun University's well-aging research to advance a human-centered model of digital inclusion, convening the university, local government, civil society, and international organizations to translate dialogue into regional action.

column4: To support healthy, active aging by giving local seniors (aged 50+) hands-on access to the arts at a university-run urban campus art center. Over 15 sessions, participants learn art theory, practice, and creation step by step—many exhibiting their own work for the first time—turning art into a lasting hobby and means of self-expression. The program also builds a sustainable well-aging culture by connecting Chosun University, Dong-gu District, and local artists with the community.
